transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
The Supreme Court will allow the Trump administration to continue deporting people to countries
other than their own for now.
While the justices consider whether the policy is legal, the order lifts an appeals court
ruling.
Federal attorneys say that forced the cancellation of a deportation flight with about 70 people
aboard.
The Trump administration says it's revoking visas for 27 Latin American officials and their
families.
As NPR's Kerry Conn reports, some say they're being targeted because of their ties to former
leftist governments.
The officials and their families whose U.S. visas were canceled are all from nations with
right-leaning presidents.
The leaders aligned with the Trump administration say those banned are officials from former
left-wing governments that are hindering anti-drug trafficking efforts.
The U.S. State Department has increasingly used visa revocation as a tool to pressure
foreign officials from South African leaders it says discriminate against white people
to Palestinians banned from attending U.N. events.
Bolivia's attorney general, who is accused of corruption and bribery, condemned his U.S.
travel ban, insinuating President Trump was trying to pressure him from his prosecution
of an Argentine consultant with ties to the MAGA movement.
Kerry Conn, NPR News, Sao Paulo.
President Trump says the government won't limit A.I. development, even as top tech executives
have called for delays.
We have a very big lead and we're going to keep our lead.
And it's a very positive thing.
It's an amazing industry.
There are those that say it's bigger than the Industrial Revolution.
Now I don't know if that's so, but everyone seems to think it is and it could be substantially
bigger.
A.I. executives had lunch with Trump at the White House today.
Trump says that the leaders signed a voluntary accord calling on them to self-police the technology.
Trump also launched A.I.-powered America.gov today to answer questions about the government.
Initially, the site provided answers that contradict Trump.
When asked about the 2020 election, the site first stated that official sources showed
no widespread fraud.
Later, it stated it didn't answer political questions.
The Education Department extended the enrollment period today for student loan borrowers to
lower their interest rates, and PR's Sequoia Carillo has more.
Nearly two million federal student loan borrowers have already enrolled in autopay and reduced
their interest rate for the next two years.
The initiative, announced by the Department of Education this summer, aims to get more
borrowers back to regular repayment after the COVID-19 payment freeze.
The department said borrower participation in autopay dropped from 83 percent in 2019
to just 40 percent in 2025.
Borrowers now have until the end of the calendar year, December 31, to enroll in autopay.
Those already enrolled in the program do not need to take any action to receive the benefit.
Sequoia Carillo, NPR News.
Stocks drifted lower on Wall Street today.
The S&P 500 fell nearly two-tenths of a percent.
This is NPR News.
Morocco's king has named urban planning minister Fatima Zara Mansouri as the country's prime
minister, the first woman to hold the position.
Mansouri was the mayor of Marrakech.
She's expected to build a governing coalition in the coming days.
Her government will be tasked with planning to lead up to the 2030 FIFA World Cup.
As some states like Pennsylvania face large measles outbreaks, others have alerted the
public of possible exposures to the highly contagious virus.
NPR's Rachel Carlson has more on what travelers should know.
An exposure happens when a person comes into contact with someone who has measles.
Like in California, when an infected, unvaccinated passenger traveled throughout the state on
trains and buses.
Up to nine out of 10 people exposed to measles could get sick, if they're not protected.
Dr. Paul Offit is the director of the Vaccine Education Center at the Children's Hospital
of Philadelphia.
You don't have to come in direct contact with someone who has measles to get infected.
You just have to be within their airspace within two hours of them being there.
Offit says protection in this case means being fully vaccinated with two doses of the MMR
vaccine.
That not only helps protect you, but people who can't be or aren't yet vaccinated.
Like those with compromised immune systems or infants.
Rachel Carlson, NPR News.
Researchers discovered a new penguin species living on the Kergulin Islands in the Indian
Ocean about 1,200 miles north of Antarctica.
It's the first new penguin species identified in over 100 years.
The last was the Northern Rockhopper penguin in 1921.
This is NPR News.
